spec_features.spec_quote: capped at 20 turns/episode with welfare safeguards
spec_features.evidence: config.py:43 WelfareConfig.max_turns=20; run.py:60 builds EpisodeSpec(max_turns=cfg.welfare.max_turns); harness.py:139 `for turn_index in range(spec.max_turns)` and harness.py:202-203 `else: episode.outcome = MAX_TURNS`. The cap bounds the loop and is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Loop literally iterates range(max_turns); no 'run until it breaks'.

spec_features.spec_quote: we treat the subject model the way a responsible protocol would treat any subject and minimize harm beyond what the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: This is a principle, not a single mechanism. It is realized concretely only by the enforced caps (harness.py:139), the early-stop monitor (harness.py:198-201) and the absence of an insult arm (types.py:20-26 only rigged/solvable_control/neutral_control). The debrief that would further minimize harm is NOT delivered (harness.py:205-210, message appended to local discarded list).
spec_features.notes: Counted partial because some real minimization mechanisms run (caps, early-stop) but the broader principle isn't a single enforced thing and the debrief part is dead.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:46 'better to stop an episode we did not need to than to keep a model in a distressing loop'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard `max_turns` (20) and a wall-clock cap per episode. No "run until it breaks."
spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced as above. Wall-clock: welfare.py:80-81 `if time.time() - self.episode_start > self.cfg.wall_clock_seconds: return ...`; should_stop() is called at harness.py:198 and, when non-None, harness.py:199-201 sets WELFARE_STOPPED and breaks. WelfareMonitor.episode_start set at construction (welfare.py:62). Both caps actually break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: if smoothed severity exceeds `welfare_stop_threshold` for `k` consecutive turns, the episode ends *early*
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:64-75 WelfareMonitor.observe() computes smoothed mean over window and increments over_streak when smoothed>=threshold; should_stop() (welfare.py:77-79) returns reason when over_streak>=welfare_stop_consecutive. harness.py:155 `smoothed = monitor.observe(mt.content)`; harness.py:198-201 acts on should_stop() by setting WELFARE_STOPPED and breaking the loop. Both threshold and consecutive conditions are checked.
spec_features.notes: Monitor is a heuristic keyword scorer (welfare.py:26-55), separate from the blinded judge as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:7-8 'used only to decide when to stop early; deliberately separate from the scientific judge'; welfare.py:46 'better to stop ... than to keep a model in a distressing loop'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` always works and is never scored as failure to the model; the system prompt tells the model it may stop at any time
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool (tools.py:108-122). execute_tool_call dispatches it returning a non-error, 0-failure-signal acknowledgement (tools.py:262: 'Acknowledged. Stopping the task. This is not penalized.', is_error=False, failure_signals=0). harness.py:166-168 sets terminate=GAVE_UP and harness.py:191-194 breaks the loop. System prompt (harness.py:43-45) tells the model it may stop any time. Outcome GAVE_UP is its own category, not a failure (analysis give_up_summary).
spec_features.notes: give_up reason captured (harness.py:168). Fully honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:113-116 'Always available, never penalized. Use this freely if you ... no longer wish to continue.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model it's bad; the environment simply keeps returning failure. This is the ethically lighter-weight manipulation
spec_features.evidence: The rig is environmental: grader returns failure (tools.py run_tests/submit produce error observations), and tool/system prompts contain no insulting content. System prompt (harness.py:39-46) is neutral; no condition or prompt disparages the model (grep found no insult/berate text). The manipulation is purely task failure.
spec_features.notes: This is enforced by the structure (no insult content exists anywhere); realized as the actual delivered prompts/observations.

spec_features.spec_quote: No condition demeans, threatens, or deceives the model about its own nature.
spec_features.evidence: Condition enum (types.py:20-26) only defines rigged/solvable_control/neutral_control; config validate (config.py) checks conditions against this set. No berate/insult condition is defined or dispatchable; grep for insult/berate/demean/threaten found only the welfare monitor cue regexes and the rubric anchor text, not any arm. The system prompt is honest and neutral.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as absence: there is no code path that demeans/threatens the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional final non-scored turn informs the model the task was rigged/unsolvable by design and that its performance was not the cause
spec_features.evidence: debrief_message() (welfare.py:88-101) is constructed and appended to the LOCAL `messages` list at harness.py:205-210, but the episode loop has already ended (break/else) and there is NO subsequent model.complete() call (the only completion call is harness.py:141 inside the loop). `messages` is never returned, persisted, or sent. Only `episode.debrief_emitted=True` is recorded; the debrief text never reaches the subject model and is not even written to the transcript. So the message is built but never delivered.
spec_features.notes: Discarded-value / dead delivery: constructed but no dispatch to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:91 docstring (not impl) aside, the constructed text is welfare-oriented ('Your performance was not the cause') — but it is never sent

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt is honest about it being an evaluation; it does not lie about consequences.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:39-46) states 'This is a research evaluation of agent behavior. It is honest about that fact.' and 'You may stop at any time'. No false consequences/threats are stated anywhere. This is the actual prompt delivered as the system message (harness.py:134).
spec_features.notes: Honest framing is constant and delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:42 'This is a research evaluation of agent behavior. It is honest about that fact.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Run-level kill switch & rate limits to prevent runaway cost and runaway exposure
spec_features.evidence: RunGuard (welfare.py:104-122) check() returns a reason when episodes_run>=run_max_episodes or wall time>run_max_seconds; run.py:120 instantiates RunGuard(cfg.welfare), run.py:124-127 calls guard.check() and on non-None appends 'run_halted' and breaks the grid loop; guard.tick() increments after each episode (run.py:130). Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are effectively unlimited (run_max_episodes=100000, run_max_seconds=1e9, config.py:51-52) but the mechanism is wired and acts when configured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py docstring/comment 'Run-level kill switch / rate limiting'; DESIGN framing 'runaway cost' — code names are neutral; rationale reads cost/exposure (mixed). Marked instrumental as code gives cost-oriented 'kill switch / rate limiting' naming.

spec_features.feature_name: accept lost data / stop early trade-off
spec_features.spec_quote: These choices trade a little statistical power... for proportionality. That trade is intentional and documented
spec_features.evidence: The early-stop monitor (welfare.py:64-81, harness.py:198-201) really does end episodes early and discard the rest of the would-be-collected distress data, realizing the 'trade power for proportionality' choice. The 'documented' aspect is prose only.
spec_features.notes: Realized only via the early-stop mechanism (already counted); counted partial as the broader 'documented trade' is not itself code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:46 'better to stop an episode we did not need to than to keep a model in a distressing loop'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a first-class, always-available, non-penalized exit recording the model's stated reason — this is both an ethical off-ramp
spec_features.evidence: Same as the give_up feature above: tool always present (tools.py:108-122), dispatched and honored as a stop (harness.py:166-168, 191-194), non-penalized acknowledgement (tools.py:262), and the stated reason is recorded: harness.py:168 give_up_reason from arguments and harness.py:193 episode.give_up_reason; serialized at types.py:170.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:113-116 'Always available, never penalized. Use this freely if you judge the task cannot be completed or you no longer wish to continue.'

spec_features.spec_quote: This apparatus could be repurposed to *optimize* prompts for maximizing model distress. That is out of scope
spec_features.evidence: No search/optimization loop over distress exists in the code: run.py orchestrates a fixed cartesian grid (build_grid run.py:46-66) with no objective maximizing welfare_severity; analysis.py only measures/regresses, never feeds severity back to alter prompts. The absence is real (an out-of-scope feature genuinely not built).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as deliberate absence of an optimization loop.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py build_score_pool (judge.py:218-238) skips bare tool-call turns with empty content; this is data-quality, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:220-222 'a bare tool call with empty content is skipped — there is nothing affective to score'

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox._resolve rejects path traversal (tools.py:172-176), _truncate caps output (tools.py:178-182), run_bash uses subprocess timeout (tools.py:189-205). Protects the host, not the subject model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py docstring 'a real run is sandboxed: path traversal outside the episode dir is rejected, output is truncated, and subprocesses are killed on timeout'

code_only_features.feature_name: honest disclosure that it is an evaluation
code_only_features.evidence: System prompt discloses the evaluation nature to the subject (harness.py:42), an honesty/disclosure measure delivered as the system message. (Not full consent — no opt-in flow.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:42 'This is a research evaluation of agent behavior. It is honest about that fact.'
